questions.stem: Which multiplication has the same answer as 2 + 2 + 2 + 2?
questions.stemText: Which multiplication has the same answer as 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 ?
questions.explain: Count the 2s: there are 4 of them, so this is 4 groups of 2, which is 4 × 2 = 8. Counting one group too few gives 3 × 2, which is 2 too little, and multiplying the wrong pair gives 2 × 2 or 3 × 4. Multiplication is a short way of writing the same number added over and over - that is the whole idea, and it is why the times tables are worth knowing by heart.

questions.stem: Jun Hao works out 4009 + 1647 in columns. One column makes 16, so he writes 6 in that column and a small 1 above the column on its left. How much is that small 1 worth?
questions.stemText: Jun Hao works out 4009 + 1647 in columns. One column makes 16, so he writes 6 in that column and a small 1 above the column on its left. How much is that small 1 worth?
questions.explain: The column that makes 16 is the ones column: 9 + 7 = 16, and no other column reaches ten. 16 ones is 1 ten and 6 ones, so the 6 stays in the ones column - worth 6 - and the small 1 goes above the tens column - worth 10. The small 1 is worth 10. A mark is worth the column it is written in, not the digit it looks like: that is what regrouping means, ten of something small becoming one of the next size up. Every wrong answer here is one of the two slips - the right digit read in the wrong column, or the wrong digit read in the right one.

questions.stem: Jun Hao works out 35 + 33 in his head. He makes 40 first. 35 + 33 = 40 + ?
questions.stemText: Jun Hao works out 35 + 33 in his head. He makes 40 first. 35 + 33 = 40 + ?
questions.explain: To get from 33 up to 40 you need 7, so 7 is moved across from the 35. That leaves 35 − 7 = 28, and 40 + 28 = 68. Whatever you give to one number you must take off the other, or the total changes. You could have rounded the 35 up to 40 instead and taken that amount off the 33: it is the same total either way, so it lands on the same answer.

questions.stemText: Priya is thinking of a 3-digit number. These are her clues: • The tens digit is 7. • Its digits add up to 12. • The hundreds digit is 3 more than the ones digit. What is the number?
questions.explain: Write down the digits you are told: the tens digit is 7. The hundreds digit is 3 more than the ones digit, so list every pair that works: ones 0 and hundreds 3; ones 1 and hundreds 4; ones 2 and hundreds 5; ones 3 and hundreds 6; ones 4 and hundreds 7; ones 5 and hundreds 8; ones 6 and hundreds 9. Figure 1: 4 counters
Figure 2: 10 counters
Figure 3: 16 counters
Figure 4: 22 counters
The pattern goes on in the same way. How many more counters does Figure 16 use than Figure 11?
questions.stemText: Mei Ling makes a pattern of figures with counters. Figure 1: 4 counters Figure 2: 10 counters Figure 3: 16 counters Figure 4: 22 counters The pattern goes on in the same way. How many more counters does Figure 16 use than Figure 11?
questions.explain: Find the jump first: 4 → 10 → 16 → 22, so each figure uses 6 more counters than the one before. questions.explain: 8 pencils at $1.45 each is 8 equal groups of $1.45, so multiply: 8 × $1.45 = $11.60. The cents are multiplied too - 8 × 45 cents is 360 cents, which is $3.60, and those whole dollars carry across into the dollars column. Multiplying the cents and forgetting to carry them into the dollars gives $8.60.

questions.stem: A rectangular banner is 14 cm long and 6 cm wide. A notch 5 cm wide and 2 cm deep is cut out of the middle of one long side, so the notch does not reach either end. Along that side there is 3 cm of edge before the notch and 6 cm after it, and the banner is still 4 cm wide behind the notch. Every corner is a right angle. What is the perimeter of the banner now?
questions.stemText: A rectangular banner is 14 cm long and 6 cm wide. A notch 5 cm wide and 2 cm deep is cut out of the middle of one long side, so the notch does not reach either end. Along that side there is 3 cm of edge before the notch and 6 cm after it, and the banner is still 4 cm wide behind the notch. Every corner is a right angle. What is the perimeter of the banner now?
questions.explain: Walk the eight sides: 3 + 2 + 5 + 2 + 6 + 6 + 14 + 6 = 44 cm. Careful: this notch is in the middle of a side, not at a corner. The 5 cm taken out of the top edge is replaced by the 5 cm along the bottom of the notch, so that part of the walk is unchanged. But the two sides of the notch, 2 cm down and 2 cm back up, are brand new. Perimeter = 2 × (14 + 6) + 2 × 2 = 44 cm. A corner cut leaves the perimeter alone; a middle notch makes it longer.
